commits.message:
docs(style): correct OSC 8 rationale — non-adjacent spans are possible

The previous comment overstated the case by claiming this pipeline "never
produces" non-adjacent OSC 8 spans for the same URL. It does — the tree
coalescer only merges *adjacent* same-link runs, so two linked segments
separated by other content emit two distinct OSC 8 pairs.

Reword to reflect the real tradeoff: dropping id= sacrifices hover-grouping
of non-adjacent same-URL spans in exchange for byte-determinism. The common
case (adjacent same-link cells sharing one wrap via the coalescer) is
unaffected.

fix(style): deterministic OSC 8 link bytes — drop module-level id counter

Style.render previously assigned each linked Style a unique _linkId from a
process-wide nextLinkId counter, leaking that id into the OSC 8 sequence as
id=N. Same logical link → different bytes across calls, which made byte-level
parity tests (rich-js + downstream cc-candybar parity harness) impossible.

The id=N parameter is optional in the OSC 8 protocol; its sole use is
hover-grouping non-adjacent spans, which the tree coalescer in render.ts
already handles by sharing a single OSC 8 wrap for adjacent same-link
segments. Omitting the id makes Style.render and segmentsToString pure
functions of their inputs — no global counter, no construction-order
dependence.

Tests added at both byte-producing seams (Style.render and segmentsToString)
that bracket the target Style with "noise" link constructions, then assert
byte-identical output for two independently-constructed same-URL Styles.

[LAW:types-are-the-program] The strongest true theorem about Style.render is
that it's a pure function of (style, text, colorSystem) — encoding the id
as part of the byte stream forced that theorem to be false; removing it
makes it true.

[LAW:no-shared-mutable-globals] The nextLinkId module-level counter was a
shared mutable global without an owning API. Deleting it (rather than
adding a reset hook) removes the type problem at its source.

[LAW:single-enforcer] Both byte producers (Style.render, segmentsToString)
now emit the same canonical OSC 8 form by construction, not by convention.

Closes rich-strip-render-d5z.1

feat(render): tree-based SGR coalescing for adjacent same-style segments (rich-strip-render-d5z) (#36)

* feat(render): coalesce adjacent same-style segments into shared SGR pairs (rich-strip-render-d5z)

The byte producer is now a single tree-shaped pass: collect non-control
non-empty pieces, partition by SGR-codes (SGR-runs), partition each run
by link (link-runs), emit one SGR open/close per run with OSC 8 link
pairs nested inside. Adjacent cells with the same SGR codes share one
wrap on the wire instead of one wrap per cell, and adjacent cells with
the same link share one OSC 8 pair inside it.

Style.toSgrCodes is extracted as the single SGR-string computation;
Style.render and the coalescer both derive from it.

Console._writeSegments and Live.refresh now route through
segmentsToString so every byte path applies the same coalescing.
segmentToString delegates to segmentsToString([seg]) so single-segment
encoding agrees byte-for-byte with the multi-segment path.

Acceptance tests in test/core/render.test.ts: 3 same-style cells → 1
SGR pair; 2 same-style + different links → 1 SGR wrap, 2 OSC 8 pairs
nested inside; 2 same-style + same link → 1 SGR wrap, 1 OSC 8 pair;
distinct-style transitions emit exactly one SGR change.

* perf(render): unified parts[] accumulator; drop empty _write call

segmentsToString now pushes every chunk (SGR / OSC 8 boundaries and
piece texts) into one parts: string[] and join("") once at the end —
avoiding the quadratic risk of += inside nested loops on large batches.
Per-link-run intermediate strings are gone; piece texts push directly
into the unified array.

Console._writeSegments encodes first, then writes only when the result
is non-empty. Recording still captures every non-control segment so
replay is unchanged.

Addresses two Copilot review findings on rich-strip-render-d5z.

* docs(render): fix dead reference to removed Console._renderSegment

Update render.ts module docstring to list the three current
delegating call sites: Console._writeSegments, Live.refresh, and
segmentToString. _renderSegment was removed when _writeSegments
started batching through segmentsToString directly.

* docs(render): NO_COLOR strips OSC 8 hyperlinks too, not just SGR

segmentToPiece already clears link bytes when colorSystem === null
(preserved from pre-coalescer Style.render behavior); make that
explicit in both the module header and RenderToStringOptions.colorSystem
JSDoc. Add a test that asserts a linked segment renders as plain text
under colorSystem === null so the doc claim stays grounded.

fix(coverage): label every allowlist entry by its actual export kind

Copilot review on PR #35 flagged that the reason string for KeyEvent
called it a "type" when src/widgets/types.ts declares it as a class.
A reader debugging a coverage failure consumes that reason string
verbatim — a wrong label is misleading guidance, not just imprecision.

The same pattern was repeated across many entries (I had labeled most
interfaces as "type" and several classes as "type"). Rather than
fix only the entry Copilot named, a derivation pass over src/ rewrote
every reason string from the actual export declaration:

  - class      → "<scope>: <Name> class"
  - interface  → "<scope>: <Name> interface"
  - type       → "<scope>: <Name> type alias"
  - const      → "<scope>: <Name> constant"
  - function   → "<scope>: <Name> function"
  - enum       → "<scope>: <Name> enum"

83 lines of labels updated. Existing parenthetical context (e.g.
"used transitively via Pretty") is preserved.

[LAW:one-source-of-truth] The src/ declaration is the canonical
description of an export's kind. A reason string that disagrees with
it is a divergent copy — fix the divergence by deriving from the
source, not by patching the copy point-by-point.

Verification: npm run lint clean; coverage verifier still green
(4/4).

chore(demos): retire flagship-per-domain spec and typing

Removes the artifacts that encoded the over-fit "exactly five flagships
with strict source-module ownership" model the previous demo-tune-up
design produced. The lit epic (rich-demos-l2x) has already been
rewritten back to the user's original ask (dedupe / expand / consolidate
/ reorganize / tweak — fewer + more interesting demos, with existing
working demos preserved until something better replaces them).

# Changes

- **Deleted `spec/demos.md`** — the 392-line spec that defined five
  flagships with rigid source-module ownership and mandated deleting the
  interactive TUIs (rich-explore, claude-sessions) to satisfy the count.
  Retired in favor of judgment-driven concrete improvements.

- **`test/coverage/coverage-allowlist.ts`** — dropped the `Flagship`
  string-literal union, the `burndown(flagship)` helper, and the
  discriminated-union `AllowlistEntry` (`{ kind: "burndown" }`
  vs `{ kind: "permanent" }`). Collapsed to one flat shape:
  `AllowlistEntry { reason: string }`. Per-flagship comment headers
  replaced with factual "-- from src/X --" sectioning. [LAW:absorbed-variance]
  — the discriminated union only had one realized case (burndown);
  collapse to one shape.

- **`test/coverage/coverage.test.ts`** — softened the file header
  comment (no longer claims to be "the keystone" of an epic; explicitly
  notes the verifier is a *floor*, not a quality measure). Updated the
  error messages and the redundant-entry detail to match the new
  AllowlistEntry shape.

- **`examples/themes-and-color-studio/index.ts`** — header comment no
  longer calls the demo "the flagship"; describes what it actually is
  (a printed-tour reference kept for the color subsystem, not a template
  for future demos). One-liner inside main() and one in-line infra
  comment updated to match.

# Verification

- npm run lint: clean
- npx vitest run: 8838 passed | 7 skipped (328 files)
- npm run themes-and-color-studio: runs to completion

# What is NOT changed

No demos under `examples/` are deleted. All existing demos
(`rich-explore`, `claude-sessions`, `rich-themes`, `rich-themes-transposed`,
`rich-theme-designer`, `rich-colors`, `rich-config`, `dropdown-demo`,
`rich-dash`, `rich-markup-plugins`, `rich-strip`, `rich-template-bindings`,
`themes-and-color-studio`, `shared`) remain on disk; their npm scripts
remain wired. Per parent epic non-goal: working demos are not deleted
before something concrete has replaced them and been judged a
replacement.
